220-ME: Evac+Chair Evac+Sled Patient Evacuation Sled
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/evac-chair-220-sled-evac-sled-evacuation-sled
Manufacturer page: https://evac-chair.com/evacuation-sleds/evac-sled/
Spec sheets: Evac+Sled data sheet (ResQMe), Evac+Chair range brochure
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: evacuation sled (80/mo, KD0). Secondary: rescue sled (100), evacuation sled for stairs (40, KD0), evacuation slide for stairs (10). Ricky's note: rescue sled has the higher volume (100) but is not the product name; use it in the body and a subhead.
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Evac+Chair Evac+Sled Patient Evacuation Sled for Floors and Stairs – 220-ME
Current H1: Evac+Chair 220-ME Evac+Sled Evacuation Sled
Subtitle: Lightweight One-Size-Fits-All Evacuation Sled with a 440 lb Capacity, Head Pillow, and Long Pulling Straps
Current subtitle: Evac+Chair 220-ME Evac+Sled Evacuation Sled
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair Evac+Sled is a lightweight patient evacuation sled that lets staff move a person who cannot walk across floors and down stairs in an emergency, such as a fire, tornado, hurricane, or act of violence. The person lies on a glideable plastic board, is held in place by safety straps and angled side flaps, and is towed by long straps at the head and feet.
It works as a rescue sled with no installation, no belay system, and no ropes: it is ready to use the moment it comes out of its wipe-clean storage bag. One size fits all, from children to adults up to 6’6” tall, and an adjustable, soft head pillow reduces head movement as the sled slides down the stairs.
Board: Glideable corrugated plastic board that slides over virtually any surface and insulates against heat; it does not need to be unrolled every few months to keep its shape
Side Flaps: Angled side board flaps keep the body in place and protect it when moving through doorways
Safety Straps: Secure patient safety straps with heavy duty hook and loop fastening
Head Pillow: Adjustable, soft pillow protects the head, reduces head movement on stairs, and fits people of different heights
Pulling Straps: Long pulling straps at the head and feet, so more than one person can help
Fit: One size fits all, for children and adults up to 6’6” tall
Use: Moves across floors and down stairs; narrow and flexible
Set-Up: No installation, belay system, or ropes needed; ready to use instantly
Weight Capacity: 440 lbs
Size Unrolled: 89”L×51”W×3”D
Weight: 4.8 lbs
Storage: Wipe-clean storage bag
Warranty: 2-year manufacturer’s warranty
Available Models and Options
220-ME – Evac+Sled: One size fits all, 440 lb capacity, 4.8 lbs
[H2] Where to Use a Rescue Sled
The Evac+Sled suits buildings where people who cannot walk, or cannot sit in an evacuation chair, may need to be moved out quickly in an emergency.
Typical applications include:
Hospitals, nursing homes, senior living, and care facilities
Schools, colleges, and childcare facilities, since it fits children and adults
Offices, theaters, libraries, hotels, and other public buildings
Emergency plans for fires, severe weather, and lockdown or violent incidents
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
What is an evacuation sled?
An evacuation sled is a flexible board or mat that a person lies on so staff can pull them to safety across the floor and down the stairs without lifting or carrying them. The Evac+Sled uses a glideable plastic board, safety straps, side flaps, and a head pillow.
How many people does it take to use the Evac+Sled?
Evac+Chair designed the Evac+Sled so that one person can move another in an emergency, and lists it for 2-person operation. The long pulling straps at the head and feet let a second person help, especially on stairs.
Can the Evac+Sled go down stairs?
Yes. The board slides down the stairs while the pillow reduces head movement, with no belay system or ropes needed.
How is the Evac+Sled different from the Evac+Chair Ulti-Mat?
The Evac+Sled is a lighter plastic board (4.8 lbs) with a 440 lb capacity. The Ulti-Mat is a padded fabric mat with standard (660 lb) and bariatric (1,000 lb) sizes.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: the primary keyword "evacuation sled" is in the H1, subtitle, first sentence, an FAQ, the meta title, and the meta description. As Ricky asked, "rescue sled" is in the body (second intro paragraph) and a subhead ("Where to Use a Rescue Sled"). "Evacuation slide for stairs" is covered by "slides down the stairs" in the intro and FAQ. "Evacuation sled for stairs" is the Ulti-Mat page's primary keyword, so I did not use that exact phrase here.
Research: the stores that rank for "evacuation sled" put the capacity and size in the product name (Global Industrial: "EvacChair 220 Evacuation Sled, 440 lb Capacity, 89"L x 51"W x 3"H"). So the 440 lb capacity is in the subtitle and meta description, and the FAQs explain what an evacuation sled is, how many people it takes, stairs, and how it differs from the Ulti-Mat.
Name: the data sheet linked from the Evac+Sled page is titled "ResQMe," with the same features and capacity, and Zoro sells it as "Evac+Chair 220M ResQme Evacuation Sled." Is the Evac+Sled the same product as the ResQMe? Our page uses "220-ME."
Operators: the Evac+Chair page says the sled "allows ONE person to safely transport another," but also lists "2 person operation." I used both, as Evac+Chair says them, in the FAQ.
Packed size: the web page says 22” x 27” x 5”, the data sheet says 20” x 24” x 5”. I left the packed size out. The unrolled size (89” x 51” x 3”), weight (4.8 lbs), and capacity (440 lbs) are the same in both.
Left out: "the ONLY transport sled that easily adapts to the passenger's size" (a comparison claim), "World's No.1," and "Successful in saving lives in 9/11."
Our current description is cut off mid-sentence ("It also comes with a") and repeats the Evac+Chair text. The new copy is fully rewritten.
Images: the 3 current images are small (800×248, 500×543, 500×322). Evac+Chair has larger photos: the sled on a staircase with a person strapped in (2498×2714) and the red storage bag (4361×2805). Would you like me to add them as "Evac-Chair-Evac-Sled-220-ME-Evacuation-Sled-on-Stairs.jpg" and "Evac-Chair-Evac-Sled-220-ME-Storage-Bag.jpg"?
Shipping weight: the variant is set to 200 lbs; the sled weighs 4.8 lbs. Is 200 lbs a placeholder?
Price: $425 with compare-at $567 (75%). No change made.
Current meta description is the general GSA pricing line. GSA is not mentioned in the description, per your note on the other tabs.
